## Natural history notes

A large carpenter bee characterized by its robust black body, shiny mostly hairless abdomen, and fuzzy yellowish thorax, often resembling a bumble bee but with a glossier rear body. In Florida, it is found in gardens, parks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, yards, farms, and other habitats with flowering plants and exposed or weathered wood for nesting. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while females excavate tunnels in wood to create brood chambers; they are important pollinators, though they may also bore into decks, fences, or wooden structures.
